name: BackX
description: Attribution methods compute importance scores for input features to explain model predictions. However, assessing the faithfulness of these methods remains challenging due to the absence of attribution ground truth to model predictions. In this work, we first identify a set of fidelity criteria that reliable benchmarks for attribution methods are expected to fulfill, thereby facilitating a systematic assessment of attribution benchmarks. Next, we introduce a Backdoor-based eXplainable AI benchmark (BackX) that adheres to the desired fidelity criteria. We theoretically establish the superiority of our approach over the existing benchmarks for well-founded attribution evaluation. With extensive analysis, we further establish a standardized evaluation setup that mitigates confounding factors such as post-processing techniques and explained predictions, thereby ensuring a fair and consistent benchmarking. This setup is ultimately employed for a comprehensive comparison of existing methods
typical_sota_score: 90–99% (task- and setup-dependent; BackX evaluations on controlled backdoor scenarios typically report very high fidelity scores)
reputation: A recent interpretability benchmark that is gaining attention for its backdoor-based ground-truth design, but it is not yet a widely standardized benchmark.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark for attribution methods; results can be sensitive to the chosen explanation setup and post-processing, and the benchmark is relatively new.
